sentences.text:
Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Mot
 Vehicles Act, 1988, to set aside the Award and Decree dated 25.07.2023 p
 in M.C.O.P.No.51 of 2022 on the file of the learned Special Subordinate 
 Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Tiruvannamalai.
For Appellant : Mr.R.Hemalatha  For Respondent : Ms.N.Lavanya  for Ms.M.Malar  JUDGMENT
Challenging the Award passed by the Tribunal, the respondent preferred this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal.

The respondent herein is the owner of the Tractor said to have been involved in a road accident on 29.10.2020.
2 . T h e l e a r n e d c o u n s e l f o r t h e a p p e l l a n t w o u l d a r g u e t h a t t h e a l l e g e d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 10/07/2025 11:33:07 am ) accident was occurred due to the negligence on the side of the claimant who drove the two wheeler in a drunken state and without wearing helmet.
The said accident was happened due to the negligence on the side of the claimant who dashed the appellant's Tractor at the back side while attempting to cross the road came in the opposite direction.
The Tribunal without fixing the contributory negligence on the part of the claimant fixed the entire liability upon the appellant, who is the owner of the Tractor and also an Agriculturist.
Hence, this appeal.

1 3.The learned counsel for the respondent would argue that at the time of accident, the Tractor was not insured and the accident was happened due to the negligence driving of the Driver of the Tractor.

sentences.text: Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly fixed the liability upon the driver of the Tractor which needs no interference.
4.A perusal of the records would reveal that on the side of the appellant, three eye witness have been examined but, the Tribunal has not accepted those evidence.

As per Ex.P.5 - Accident Register copy dated 29.10.2020 and the additional documents now produced before this Court by the appellant, it reveals that immediately after the accident, when the claimant was admitted in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 10/07/2025 11:33:07 am ) the hospital and the hospital authority noted that the claimant was under the influence of alcohol.
Furthermore, he came from the opposite direction, thereby the accident was occurred.
Therefore, there is a contributory negligence on the side of the claimant also.
But, the Tribunal failed to take note of the said fact.
Hence, the objections raised by the appellant is sustainable one.
5.Considering all these facts and circumstances of this case, this Court is inclined to modify the Award passed by the Tribunal by fixing the contributory negligence upon the respondent/claimant.
Accordingly, 40% of contributory negligence is fixed on the respondent/claimant and 60% of contributory negligence is fixed on the side of the appellant.
In all other respects, the Award remains unaltered.
Out of total compensation of Rs.1,55,000/-, the appellant is directed to pay 60% towards contributory negligence of Rs.93,000/- to the claimant.
6.Accordingly, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is disposed of.

The appellant is directed to deposit a sum of Rs.93,000/- with interest @7.5% per annum, less the amount already deposited, with proportionate accrued interest and costs, to the credit of M.C.O.P.No.51 of 2022 on the file of the learned Special Subordinate Judge, Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Tiruvannamalai,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

On such deposit,
the claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire award amount with proportionate accrued interest and costs by making necessary applications.
The claimant is directed to pay the Court fee for the compensation amount, if required.
The Tribunal below shall not disburse the amount till such time as proof of payment of Court Fee has been produced by the claimant.
No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
